setting: If a file can't be read well
effect: The default blocked the whole files run in R1 because one ordinary government PDF (Census P60-279) was flagged for malformed tables. 'Publish the other files and show warnings' published it with warnings (R1w), but it does not publish the others when a required file cannot be read at all: R3b (OCR off) still failed the whole run. On websites (R5) it changed nothing because no page failed.
recommendation: Keep the choice, but fix what it does: 'publish the others' should exclude any unreadable file, not only files marked optional (finding X3). Reconsider the default once X1 and X2 are fixed.

effect: Turning it off made the scanned report unreadable and failed the whole files run (and every scan question). Leaving it on costs nothing for text PDFs: OCR ran only on the image-only pages.
recommendation: Always run OCR when the server supports it; show a note only when OCR is unavailable.

where: Extract panel (visible when OCR is on)
effect: Only English sources and the English language pack were used.
recommendation: Keep; it matters for non-English scans. Test with a non-English scan before changing it.

effect: Retrieval on the three files: Hit@5 16/19 with v1 vs 17/19 with v2 (v1 lost the scan's luminance-range question; both miss the same two Census table questions), Hit@1 8 vs 9. Answers: identical on the 8 file questions (6 correct, 1 correct-abstain, 1 wrong-abstain each). v2 also keeps headings and section paths that v1 does not.
recommendation: Keep v2 as the default and the upgrade as the only control; no new user setting.

effect: No change in any retrieval result, structure or answer on the scanned report.
recommendation: Fix at 200 DPI; revisit only if a real low-quality scan shows a difference.

effect: No change: the scan had 10 pages. It only matters for scans longer than 50 pages, where the default would fail the file.
recommendation: Raise the default to the server maximum (100) and keep it in Advanced.

effect: No page came close: OCR took about 1-2 s per page.
recommendation: Keep as a fixed server safety limit, not a user setting.

effect: The real scan was upright; earlier synthetic tests showed rotation is needed for sideways scans and costs little.
Auto handled the two-column paper, the report and the scan; Auto picked layout analysis on every text page.

setting: Table evidence (Structured + Markdown / Markdown / Plain text)
effect: No change in any retrieval result (Hit@1 24, Hit@5 42 both); 684 vs 718 chunks. It does not apply to websites.

setting: Quality thresholds (empty pages, characters, OCR confidence, reading order, malformed tables)
effect: 'Fail on malformed tables' is what blocked the Census report; 'suspicious reading order' only warned on the BERT paper and the report.
recommendation: Keep for experts; make the malformed-table check warn, not fail, until X2 is fixed.

effect: All sources were English; no language findings.

The only setting that moved results both ways: Hit@1 26 vs 24 and Hit@5 42 vs 42 overall; MDN improved (Hit@5 6 to 7, Hit@1 4 to 6), the scan improved at rank 1, two Wikipedia questions were gained and two lost, one BERT question was lost. Doubles the chunks and the embedding cost.
recommendation: Keep 600 / 800 / 80 as the default and keep chunk size visible in the Chunk stage.
